extra_misconceptions.fact: Standard automation follows fixed, pre-programmed rules and triggers without learning from new data.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every automated workflow uses machine learning to adapt its behavior during execution.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Modern chatbots are narrow AI systems trained to predict text patterns rather than think across all human domains.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Current conversational chatbots are examples of general AI because they discuss many topics.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Basic programming uses explicit human-written rules, whereas machine learning discovers patterns directly from training data.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Basic programming and machine learning both require a developer to write explicit rules for every output.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Data consists of raw facts and measurements, while a database is the organized system built to store and query that data.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A database and raw data are identical concepts in artificial intelligence systems.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a machine learning model when its training data contains systematic errors or missing values?
Under what condition does an automated workflow require a trigger before executing its sequence of tasks?
Which technical capability separates an autonomous AI agent from a simple rule-based chatbot script?
Why does a chess-playing engine qualify as narrow AI rather than general or superintelligent AI?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Everyday consumer features like smartphone face unlock, spam filters, and voice assistants run AI models constantly.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Artificial intelligence only runs inside specialized robotics labs or cloud supercomputers.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Effective workplace AI flags patterns and anomalies so qualified human professionals can make faster, informed decisions.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Workplace AI systems are designed to replace all human judgment in medical and financial roles.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Submitting AI-written work as your own violates academic integrity, whereas using AI to quiz yourself supports real learning.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Using a generative AI tool to write an entire school essay counts as legitimate student research.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Modern spam filters use machine learning classifiers that adapt to new phishing wording and sender behavior.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Email spam filters rely only on a fixed blocklist of known sender addresses to catch junk mail.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a navigation app's route prediction when live traffic sensor data suddenly changes?
Which signal tells you that a workplace software tool uses adaptive AI instead of a static lookup table?
Why is it dangerous to submit an AI-generated school summary without verifying each cited source?
Where should a student set the boundary between using AI as a study tutor and committing academic dishonesty?

extra_misconceptions.fact: A timer-triggered coffee maker is deterministic automation because it follows a fixed schedule without learning.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A programmable coffee maker that brews at 6:00 AM is an example of artificial intelligence.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Payroll automation calculates paychecks using strict mathematical formulas and legal tax tables with zero guesswork.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Automated workplace payroll systems decide employee tax rates by analyzing historical trends.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Rule-based automation remains the safest, fastest choice whenever a task requires repeatable and predictable execution.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Deterministic automation is obsolete now that machine learning models are widely available.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Standard sliding doors use a simple motion or infrared sensor trigger that opens the door whenever anything enters range.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: An automatic sliding grocery store door uses computer vision AI to decide who should enter.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a home thermostat's heating cycle when the room temperature crosses its set threshold?
Under what condition does a deterministic factory conveyor script fail without human intervention?
Which everyday school task benefits more from a scheduled calendar reminder than from a predictive AI model?
Why is it dangerous to deploy an automated billing script without testing its error-stopping conditions first?

extra_misconceptions.fact: AI models inherit and amplify any historical prejudices or sampling gaps present in their human-collected training data.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Mathematical algorithms are naturally neutral and cannot produce biased or unfair outcomes.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Many public AI services log user inputs and may use those conversations to train future models unless privacy settings block it.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Deleting a chat window immediately erases your private prompts from a public AI provider's servers.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Human developers, deploying organizations, and operators retain ethical responsibility for the systems they build and use.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: When an autonomous system causes harm, the software itself is legally and morally accountable.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A model with high average accuracy can still fail at much higher rates for smaller, underrepresented demographic groups.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: High overall accuracy on a test dataset proves that an AI model is fair to every group of users.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a hiring algorithm's fairness when its historical training data underrepresents certain groups?
Why is it dangerous to upload personal medical records or troop rosters into a public AI tool?
Under what condition must a human reviewer override an automated AI decision in healthcare or lending?
Which specific rule in your personal ethical guidelines protects user privacy before a prompt is sent?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Deepfakes include synthetic audio voice clones and fabricated photos used in financial scams, bullying, and misinformation.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Deepfakes only involve swapping faces in Hollywood movies or celebrity parody videos.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Accessible consumer software can clone a person's voice or likeness from just a few seconds of public social media audio.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Creating a realistic voice or video deepfake still requires millions of dollars in studio hardware.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Victims should document URLs and screenshots immediately, tell a trusted adult, and report the content for platform removal.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The best response to being targeted by a malicious deepfake is to delete the evidence and stay silent.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Modern generative models hide many visual flaws, so verifying the source through a separate trusted channel is essential.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Human eyes and ears can reliably spot every synthetic video or cloned voice without verification tools.

extra_socratic_questions: Which visual or audio artifact in a video call suggests that the speaker might be a synthetic deepfake?
Why is it dangerous to share or forward a suspected deepfake video even if you are warning friends about it?
What evidence should a victim preserve before reporting a malicious deepfake to a parent, school, or platform?
Under what condition can a voice-cloning deepfake trick a family member into sending money or passwords?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Language models predict likely word sequences and can hallucinate plausible-sounding falsehoods that require fact-checking.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A confident, well-written paragraph from a language model guarantees that the underlying facts are true.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Clear prompts specify context, target audience, constraints, and desired output format to guide the model accurately.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Effective prompt engineering means typing the shortest possible one-word or two-word question.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Iterative refinement, where you critique the first draft and add missing constraints, routinely improves AI output quality.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: If an AI model gives a weak answer on the first try, the model is incapable of helping with that task.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Pre-trained models have knowledge cutoffs and cannot know recent events unless connected to live search or provided context.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: AI models learn new facts instantaneously from every single prompt without any training cutoff limits.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to the accuracy of an AI response when you add role, audience, and format constraints to your prompt?
Why does a large language model sometimes invent fake book titles or false historical dates with high confidence?
Under what condition does providing two or three concrete examples inside a prompt improve the generated output?
What verification step confirms that a step-by-step campout checklist generated by AI is safe to follow?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Successful AI projects start with a clear objective, a data collection plan, and an ethical risk review before coding.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Building a practical AI project begins with writing code before defining the problem or checking data quality.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Evaluating on training data hides overfitting; you must test the model on held-out examples it has never seen before.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Testing a machine learning model on its own training examples is the most reliable way to measure performance.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Clean, representative, and accurately labeled data matters far more to project success than raw volume of bad data.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: More training data automatically fixes a project even when the labels are noisy, biased, or irrelevant.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Even small community projects must protect user privacy, avoid biased recommendations, and state their limitations clearly.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Ethical review only matters for commercial tech companies and is unnecessary for a small community Scout project.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to your project's test results if you evaluate your model on the exact same data used to train it?
Which metric or failure log in your project plan tells you whether your AI tool solves the community need?
Where should you document edge cases and ethical risks before deploying your project for real users?
Why must you obtain counselor approval and check data permissions before collecting community dataset samples?

extra_misconceptions.fact: AI careers span data engineering, automation technician roles, product management, and ethics, with varied education paths.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every career in artificial intelligence requires a doctoral degree in advanced theoretical mathematics.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Employers also value communication, ethical judgment, teamwork, and domain knowledge to translate AI into safe solutions.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Technical coding skill is the only qualification employers evaluate when hiring artificial intelligence professionals.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Healthcare, agriculture, manufacturing, finance, and public service organizations all hire AI and automation specialists.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Artificial intelligence and automation jobs only exist inside software companies in major tech hubs.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Rapidly evolving AI tools and standards require continuous learning, updated certifications, and hands-on practice.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Completing a single college degree provides all the technical knowledge needed for a thirty-year AI career.

extra_socratic_questions: Which daily responsibilities separate a machine learning engineer from an AI ethics and policy specialist?
What happens to an automation engineer's career readiness if they stop learning after earning one certification?
Where can a high school student gain hands-on portfolio experience in AI before paying for a college degree?
Under what condition does domain expertise in medicine or agriculture matter as much as coding in an AI career?
